sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
Before learning frameworks, students should implement the underlying execution loop.

We will use a local synthetic order database to avoid requiring an actual business API.

scenario.title: Scenario — Part — 7. Build an AI agent from scratch — Without LangChain
scenario.situation: principal="customer_1" ) print(result) This is an educational implementation using the Chat Completions tool-calling interface. It demonstrates bounded execution, strict argument validation and owner-scoped tools, but still needs request-wide deadlines, provider error handling, token accounting, output verification and telemetry before pr

steps.label: Goal
steps.narration: The agent receives a user goal and must decide what information or tools are required.

steps.label: Reason
steps.narration: The model plans the next action instead of answering blindly.

steps.label: Act / tool
steps.narration: The agent calls an authorized tool or function with structured arguments.

steps.label: Observe
steps.narration: Usage, cost, latency, and traces are recorded for FinOps and incident response.

steps.label: Decide
steps.narration: The loop continues, escalates to a human, or finishes with a grounded answer.

7.7 Practical assignment — Project 1
sections.body:
Extend the agent with shipment tracking, policy retrieval and support ticket preparation.

Your tests should prove that:

- An authorized customer can retrieve their own order.
- Another customer's order is unavailable.
- Unknown tools cannot execute.
- Invalid arguments are rejected.
- Repeated calls stop when the step budget is exhausted.
- A tool error is not presented as a successful business operation.
